The collapse of the Soviet bloc accelerated this integration, culminating in the signing of the historic Maastricht Treaty in February 1992, which formally established the European Union. The treaty laid the groundwork for a common foreign and security policy, cooperation on justice and home affairs, and the creation of a single European currency, the Euro, which was launched in January 2002.
